page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. The instance demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 81293.61 and a passmark CPU score of 55910.68. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top tier for both cached small block reads at 4502.68 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 215.93 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression both falling into the bottom 25 percent of tested servers.

Given the high memory density, fast local NVMe storage, and 100 Gbps network throughput, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring massive memory capacity and high-speed data transfer without the overhead of external storage. It is well-suited for large-scale Redis deployments, where it achieves 75.03 million operations per second, high-throughput static web serving, and memory-intensive database operations. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or complex real-time LLM text generation.
